reports.name: KPMG and REC, UK Report on Jobs November 2026 (October data)
reports.reason: Public press release read in full; index values and full report are subscription-only via S&P Global (permanent gate).
reports.method_sample: Monthly survey of a panel of around 400 UK recruitment and employment consultancies, data collected 12 to 26 October 2026, seasonally adjusted diffusion indices
reports.reader_fit: High for UK readers: first fall in permanent placements in four months, pre-Budget caution, candidate supply up sharply. Free summary is linkable; no index numbers in the free release.

key_figures.claim: UK permanent placements fell for the first time in four months
key_figures.verbatim quote: The number of people placed into permanent jobs across the UK fell for the first time in four months in October

key_figures.claim: UK temp billings fell for the first time since March
key_figures.figure: first fall since March, after six months of rises
key_figures.verbatim quote: Temp billings also fell after rising for six consecutive months.

key_figures.claim: UK vacancies fell at the softest pace in over two years
key_figures.verbatim quote: Overall vacancies decline at softest pace since August 2024

key_figures.claim: Candidate supply rose sharply
key_figures.figure: growth picked up from September's three-year low
key_figures.verbatim quote: The supply of candidates rose sharply in October, with the rate of growth picking up from September's three-year low.

key_figures.claim: Permanent demand up in most sectors, led by IT and Engineering
key_figures.verbatim quote: Six of the ten monitored job categories recorded increased demand for permanent workers in October, led by the IT & Computing and Engineering sectors.

reports.name: SIA | Bullhorn Staffing Indicator, week ending October 31, 2026
reports.reason: Full weekly report text and both index tables were public on the SIA report page (also mirrored on bullhorn.com); only a members-only download beneath it was not opened.
reports.method_sample: Weekly hours worked by temporary workers across a sample of US staffing firms using Bullhorn, weighted and benchmarked to BLS data; index base week ending 13 Jan 2019; last 4 weeks preliminary
reports.reader_fit: Medium: US agency and staffing readers; a clean weekly number. Note the following week's edition is on hold for data review.

key_figures.claim: US staffing hours up 12% year over year, a 2026 high
key_figures.verbatim quote: The US Staffing indexed value was 110 for the week ending October 31st (“last week measured”). US Staffing hours were up 12% compared to a year ago and up 1.3% on a week-over-week sequential basis.

key_figures.claim: Professional staffing hours up 10% YoY
key_figures.verbatim quote: The Professional Staffing indexed value was 129 for the same week. Professional hours were up 10% compared to a year ago; and were up 2.1% on a week-over-week sequential basis.

key_figures.claim: IT staffing hours up 7% YoY
key_figures.verbatim quote: The IT staffing indexed value was 120 for the week ending October 31st, up 7% compared to a year ago and up 1.9% on a week-over-week sequential basis

key_figures.claim: Industrial staffing hours up 18% YoY
key_figures.verbatim quote: The Industrial staffing indexed value was 100 for the same week, up 18% compared to a year ago and up 0.5% on a week-over-week sequential basis.

key_figures.claim: Office/clerical still below 2025
key_figures.verbatim quote: the Office/Clerical staffing indexed value was 64 for the same week, down 7% compared to a year ago but up 1.6% on a week-over-week sequential basis.

reports.name: UK Labour Market Snapshot, October 2026
reports.reason: Public blog post read in full via the site's public posts feed; no gate.
reports.method_sample: Indeed Job Postings Index (seasonally adjusted, 7-day trailing average, 1 Feb 2020 = 100) and Indeed Wage Tracker, plus ONS data; data to 16 October 2026
reports.reader_fit: High for UK readers: free, quotable posting and pay numbers, regional and city splits.

key_figures.claim: UK job postings 31% below pre-pandemic
key_figures.verbatim quote: UK job postings on Indeed edged up 0.3% in the month to 16 October, but still sit 31% below early 2020 levels.

key_figures.claim: UK postings down 7.5% year over year
key_figures.verbatim quote: the year-over-year decline little changed at -7.5% (from -7.8% in mid-September).

key_figures.claim: UK posted wage growth cooled to 3.5%, now only matching inflation
key_figures.verbatim quote: Posted wage growth has cooled to 3.5% over the year to September 2026, down from around 4% through the spring and summer.

key_figures.claim: Only 7 of 49 sectors have postings above pre-pandemic baseline
key_figures.verbatim quote: Of the 49 categories we tracked, 7 have postings above the baseline.

key_figures.claim: UK redundancy notifications at highest since 2020
key_figures.verbatim quote: Notifications rose to 50,904 in September, the highest since October 2020

reports.name: 2026 Recruiter Nation Report: The Recruiter Recalibration, Resetting the Hiring Playbook
reports.reason: Full report behind a free email form (Marketo) on the Lever landing page; figures taken from Employ's PR Newswire release (14 Oct 2026) and Employ's Jobvite blog (5 Nov 2026).
reports.method_sample: Survey of more than 1,200 US-based HR recruiters and managers by Zogby Analytics for Employ, August 2026; 19th annual edition
reports.reader_fit: High: candidate fraud, AI-polished CVs as top stressor, AI time savings stalling, recruiter AI guidelines. Free email signup, so acceptable under the access rule. Vendor survey: name Employ as the source.

key_figures.claim: AI-polished resumes are the top recruiter stressor for the first time
key_figures.verbatim quote: For the first time in the 19-year history of this survey, the biggest source of recruiter stress is tied to AI. AI-polished resumes now top the list at 33%, overtaking a lack of qualified candidates

key_figures.claim: Confirmed AI-driven candidate fraud rising
key_figures.verbatim quote: More than one-quarter of organizations (27%) report confirmed AI-driven candidate fraud, up from 23% in 2025.

key_figures.claim: AI use widespread but few have shifted most of their time to higher-value work
key_figures.figure: 68% use AI; 18% shifted more than half their time
key_figures.verbatim quote: Sixty-eight percent of recruiters use AI alongside their recruiting technology, and 66% say it has made their jobs easier. Yet only 18% say more than half of their time has shifted from administrative work to higher-value tasks.

key_figures.claim: Hiring widespread but smaller in scale
key_figures.figure: 43% made 25 or fewer hires, up from 20%
key_figures.verbatim quote: In 2026, 43% of organizations reported making 25 or fewer hires over the past 12 months. In 2025, that figure was just 20%.

key_figures.claim: Formal AI guidelines for recruiters
key_figures.verbatim quote: Nearly half of HR decision-makers (47%) have formal guidelines for how recruiters use AI, while another 30% are developing them.

key_figures.claim: Satisfaction with primary recruiting systems fell
key_figures.verbatim quote: Satisfaction with primary recruiting systems fell from 82% in 2025 to 69% this year
